q is fast and s is slow in the intended operating regime.
All displayed KL laws share domination and positive support where required.
Every continuum claim fixes a mesh family, topology, base measure, boundary data, and gauge treatment.

claims.statement: For every fixed finite number N of section-valued agents over a finite lattice or a compact contextual base with a refining lattice family, construct an ELBO-founded PIFB2 theory in which fast belief sections q_i are recognition densities, slow model sections s_i are typed parameter-recognition laws or deterministic parameters, and transported peer interactions use KL(q_i||(Omega_ij)_#q_j); distinguish exact time-lagged conditional, configuration-law, and emergent empirical-measure realizations; begin with arbitrary compact closed subgroups of GL(K,R), and state the additional obligations for a full GL(K,R) extension and for deterministic or process-law continuum limits.
claims.quantifiers: For every fixed finite N >= 1; lattice refinement h->0 is separate from any later N->infinity limit.
claims.falsifier: Closure requires the simultaneous-peer emergence, adiabatic, residual, continuum, and full-GL obligations.

claims.statement: q is correctly typed as a fast recognition density or approximate posterior; a law-valued s is a slow parameter-recognition or model-belief section rather than the generative kernel itself.
claims.quantifiers: The stated PIFB2 operating regime and the cited Friston variational formulations.
claims.falsifier: A primary source or live definition contradicts this terminology or timescale status.

claims.statement: The lagged source-label construction yields categorical KL plus weighted transported peer KL exactly.
claims.quantifiers: Every finite nonempty source set with strictly positive normalized source and recognition rows, normalized recognition and transported state laws, and common domination.
claims.falsifier: An admitted positive finite example violates the direct KL expansion.

claims.statement: Minimizing the exact state VFE over an unrestricted fast recognition law yields negative log slow-conditional evidence; restricted families retain the posterior-KL gap.
claims.quantifiers: Every normalized model with positive finite conditional evidence and admitted posterior.
claims.falsifier: A normalized model violates the posterior KL identity.

claims.statement: Every compact linear subgroup of GL(K,R) preserves some positive inner product and is conjugate into O(K).
claims.quantifiers: Every finite-dimensional real compact linear group.
claims.falsifier: Exhibit a compact linear subgroup for which Haar averaging fails to produce a positive invariant inner product.

claims.statement: The same-time reciprocal transported peer interaction is derived noncircularly from an independently specified microscopic law.
claims.quantifiers: The intended finite-N reciprocal agent system.
claims.falsifier: A fixed-law construction or empirical-measure LDP verifies it; contemporaneous Q-dependence or circular Gibbs insertion defeats it.

claims.statement: The intended fast q and slow s dynamics admit a valid adiabatic elimination with the stated effective slow action.
claims.quantifiers: The intended coupled fast-slow flow over its admitted parameter regime.
claims.falsifier: Loss of uniqueness, attraction, normal hyperbolicity, or uniform scale separation defeats it.

claims.statement: For fixed finite N, the selected compact-group lattice actions converge to the intended continuum section action.
claims.quantifiers: The declared refining lattice family and continuum topology.
claims.falsifier: Failure of equicoercivity, liminf, recovery, residual convergence, or gauge compactness defeats it.

claims.statement: A normalized coercive full-GL(K) theory with physical SPD/nonmetricity modes and gauge-invariant complexity observables exists for the intended model.
claims.quantifiers: The intended full noncompact gauge extension.
claims.falsifier: Infinite gauge volume, metric degeneration, or representative-dependent observables defeat it.
